event_confirmation: Company announcement of 2026-09-30 (Q3 2026 results before market hours Tue 2026-10-27, call 09:00 CT), seen via QuiverQuant's reproduction (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Central+Bancompany%2C+Inc.+Announces+Third+Quarter+2026+Earnings+Release+and+Conference+Call) and StockAnalysis's news list (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/CBC, item dated Sept 30, 2026). The IR site centralbancompany.gcs-web.com returned 403, so the original release was not opened. The date fits the company's cadence: earlier 8-K item 2.02 filings came on Tuesdays 2026-01-27, 04-28 and 08-04. Earnings Whispers' Nov 3 is a vendor projection.
conviction_note: The findings are small and point both ways (sum +0.2): a Fed hike that helps an asset-sensitive bank with 4.40% NIM and 28.6% CET1 of mostly cash, against peer deposit-cost creep and a stock already at its 52-week high and at the consensus target after a +7.4% week that was mostly KRE beta (+5.4%). The name's three prints moved a median 0.63%, so the scaled number sits at p_up 50 on a 2.0% abs move. The two measurements roughly agree: both are close to zero.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS $0.49. Benzinga gives $0.49 EPS and $288.6M revenue (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CBC/earnings-forecasts); TradersUnion gives about $0.49 from 5 analysts and $291.6M revenue (https://tradersunion.com/stocks/earnings/cbc-usd/). Two sources agree on EPS. Q2 was $0.47 against a $0.48 estimate; Q1 was $0.46 against $0.44. The company gives no numeric guidance.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest on 2026-09-30 was 9,097,041 shares, up 52.8% from 5,953,550 on 09-15 and roughly tripled since April; days to cover 4.08 (https://equibles.com/stocks/cbc/shortinterest, accessed 2026-10-26). MarketBeat puts that at 11.14% of float (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CBC/short-interest/); against 239.5M shares outstanding it is 3.8%, and the float is small because the family controls the company. The 10-15 figure publishes on 10-26 and was not seen; Equibles' model estimates 9.67M. Part of the September build plausibly reflects ETF arbitrage after CBC joined the S&P Banks Select Industry Index, the index behind KRE (Yahoo headline, unverified). The options chain is empty in the baseline, so there is no skew or implied move. Unusual Whales quotes about ±8.09%, which is unreliable on an empty chain. The 5-day run-up is +7.27%; the stock is at its 52-week high, 52% above the 52-week low.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds target 25bp, to 3.75-4.00%, on 2026-09-16 (12-0). On the Q2 call (2026-08-04) Central Bancompany's management had planned for a 'gradual easing of the prime rate'. CBC is asset sensitive: NIM 4.40% (up from 4.32% in Q1), deposit cost 1.10%, and $1.9B of excess capital held as cash at the holding company. The hike adds only about two weeks to Q3 NII, but it gives a basis for a constructive Q4 NII/NIM tone on the call. The company gives no numeric guide, so the market has no published number to compare against.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior guide. NIM rose 8bp in Q2 and the stock moved +0.63% on 2026-08-04; Q1's print (-1.97%) also showed NIM expansion.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced at sector level. KRE rose from 69.26 to 73.00 (+5.4%) between Oct 19 and Oct 26, and CBC rose 7.4%. If it were fully priced, CBC would be expected to underperform on a NIM-up quarter, and the stock already sits at the consensus target ($34.60). What is not public is CBC's own Q4 NII trajectory, because it gives no guide. The caveat is also on the record: on the Q2 call management said it was 'marginally reducing asset sensitivity' and that loan spreads compress when rates rise sharply (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CBC/Q22026), so the size is small.
findings.independence: Peers that reported after CBC last spoke support it. BOKF core NIM rose 8bp to 3.21% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000875357/000087535726000054/a20260930bokfex99.htm). CBSH's underlying NIM rose 5bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022356/000002235626000209/cbsh09302026ex991.htm). Regions said repricing lags after the September hike should modestly lift Q4 NII (https://www.earningswhispers.com/transcript/RF). This is macro-to-company transmission: CBC has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said about $1.3B of loans reprice in 2H26, rolling off a 5.8% yield, while the Q2 portfolio loan yield was 6.24%. It also repositioned $210M of securities from about 2.0% into about 4.5% (deck). Those are mechanical tailwinds for Q3 NII after Q2's +$4.2M QoQ (to $212.8M). Q2 period-end loans grew about 6.5% annualized ex consumer runoff, above the average balance, which gives Q3 average loans a head start.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NII and NIM have risen on each of the three prints (+0.63%, -1.97%, -0.33%), so growth inside the expected range has not bought the stock anything.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is in management's own public commentary, and consensus of $0.49 (from $0.47) already assumes NII growth. It is filed because it supports a small beat on the bar rather than a miss. If it were unpriced, consensus would sit at or below Q2's $0.47.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K and deck are the same company's documents (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002065601/000162828026052174/investordeckq22026final.htm), so the source is not independent. BOKF's Q3 shows the same back-book repricing effect at a peer (about $770M of securities at 3.3% reinvested near 5.1%).

findings.finding: Funding pressure in Q3. Management said public fund deposits decline seasonally in Q3 and rise in Q4. Peers that reported in October saw deposit costs creep up after the hike: CBSH interest-bearing deposit cost rose to 1.63% from 1.57%, with average deposits down 1.3%; EFSC's cost of deposits rose 1bp, to 1.54%. CBC's Q2 cost of deposits was 1.10%, down 3bp; a reversal would cap Q3 NIM expansion.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 average deposits fell 1.1% QoQ (seasonal) and the stock moved +0.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: The seasonal public-funds decline was guided, so that part is priced. Peer deposit-cost creep after the hike is a proxy, and CBC's Missouri deposit base has a lower beta than CBSH's. If the market had priced a funding squeeze, CBC would not have outrun KRE last week.
findings.independence: EFSC Q3 2026 exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001025835/000102583526000185/ex991financialstatementsan.htm): deposit cost +1bp. The seasonal statement comes from CBC's own Q2 call (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CBC/Q22026). Peer data is a proxy.

findings.finding: Midwest peer prints were mixed, not clean beats. BOKF's NIM expanded but it cut its full-year fee outlook to over $800M (from $820-845M) and trimmed NII guidance. CBSH Q3 EPS was $1.08, below Q2's $1.10. EFSC earned $1.14, below its Q2 per-share level, with ROAA flat at 0.95%. Prints in CBC's footprint did not give the sector an easy read-through for upside on the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured peer-to-CBC reaction history; CBC has three prints.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (URL path carries no date; BOKF Q3 2026 8-K)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: KRE rose through these prints, which says the sector read them as fine. It is filed as a small offset because BOKF (Oklahoma, a CBC target market) and CBSH (Missouri) are the nearest comparables, and neither printed a clean upside.
findings.independence: The CBSH 8-K is a separate document (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000022356/000002235626000209/cbsh09302026ex991.htm), but it shares the CBSH source with the deposit finding: two readings of one document. Here the CBSH EPS line is used; there, its deposit line.

findings.finding: Valuation ceiling. The stock is at a 52-week high ($34.80 intraday on Oct 26), 28% above the $27.13 average Q2 buyback price, and at the 5-analyst consensus target ($34.60). Morgan Stanley downgraded it to Equal Weight from Overweight in mid-September (target $36). This makes a sell-the-news reaction to an in-line print somewhat more likely, and it makes buybacks under the $100M 'opportunistic' authorization less likely at these prices.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 (04-28) beat EPS $0.46 against $0.44 and the stock fell 1.97%, so a beat has been sold before.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not new information; it is a statement about the bar for upside. If the market had a more bullish view, targets would have moved above spot. Short interest has risen into the print (9.1M, DTC 4.1), which argues for shrinking this negative, so it is kept small.
findings.independence: Morgan Stanley downgrade (https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8905169, undated in snippet). Q2 deck buyback price $27.13 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002065601/000162828026052174/investordeckq22026final.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest built steadily into the print: 9,097,041 shares at 09-30, up from 5.95M at 09-15, 4.59M at 08-31 and about 1.9M in mid-April; 4.1 days to cover. That is 11% of the float by MarketBeat's float count. The +7.4% move since Oct 19 came on above-average volume (1.53M shares on Oct 20, against a 20-day average of 0.82M), which is consistent with some covering into a clean print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was much lower around the three prior prints (about 0.46M in Jan, about 2.2M in Apr, about 5.1M in Jul), so there is no reaction history at this level.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, but a squeeze needs a catalyst, and the print is one. Part of the build is plausibly ETF or index-arbitrage hedging after the S&P Banks Select Industry Index inclusion rather than directional shorts, which caps the size. If the shorts had already covered, the 10-15 figure would show a drop, and that figure was not seen.
findings.independence: MarketBeat shows the same FINRA data, 11.14% of float (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/CBC/short-interest/), so it is not independent.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew. The 9.1% 20-day and 7.3% 5-day run-ups put the stock at its 52-week high, mostly with KRE. The small positives (rate hike, repricing, short interest) agree with the run-up and are therefore partly priced. The valuation-ceiling and peer findings cut against it, which nets to roughly zero and keeps p_up at 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 3 / rule 5: the rate-hike finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3. Its own caveat (management reducing asset sensitivity; loan spreads compress in sharp rate rises) and macro-to-company transmission that CBC has not confirmed both reach the number.
Rule 7: the valuation-ceiling negative cut from -0.3 to -0.2, because short interest is building (9.1M, DTC 4.1, 11% of float by MarketBeat).
Rule 6: the bar was checked against two agreeing sources ($0.49, Benzinga and TradersUnion), so no cap was applied. The lock-up is outside the window and sits in rejected_candidates.
Rule 1: with a 0.63% median reaction and a sold beat in Q1, the scaled number stays at p_up 50; abs_move is 2.0%, set above the 3-print median because the history is thin.
